prediction.likelyOutcome: Liability (the fact of a compensable taking) is not in dispute; the fight is purely about amount. Given that both experts share the same highest-and-best-use premise and differ mainly on per-acre rates and on how much the 43-meter access restriction actually degrades the western parcel's value, expect the Court of Claims to award total just compensation somewhere between the State's floor (value of the land physically taken, no severance) and claimant's aggressive 'surplus acreage' theory — with the collateral estoppel ruling on landlocked status and the State's specific multifamily-development testimony pulling the likely result toward the lower-to-middle part of that range rather than claimant's high end.

outcome.description: After a four-day January 2018 trial the Court of Claims credited the State's appraiser (with its own adjustments, preappropriation value $52,339 per acre or $1,662,810), found the western remainder's post-taking highest and best use was multifamily residential, and awarded KKS $744,500 in direct and consequential damages. The Third Department affirmed the amended judgment on October 29, 2020. (An earlier award of $532,000 had been reversed in 2014.)
